summary: Generated 20 SVG panels at N=1000000 (continued-fraction subrange 12000). No candidate can be honestly called mathematically undiscovered from this run. The strongest project-native survivor is #7/#8, the Dyadic-Mobius/E2 transform diagnostic; the strongest mathematical visuals are #3 and #4, but both are famous open 1/4-exponent problems.

candidates.name: Squarefree count Q(x)
candidates.note: The level line is real, but the 1/4 exponent question is a named classical squarefree-error problem, not an undiscovered object.

candidates.name: Liouville L(x)
candidates.note: Distinct from Mertens in the app, but the object and its failure modes are classical; no new discovery claim survives.

candidates.name: Dirichlet divisor Delta(x)
candidates.note: This is one of the best visual 1/4 siblings, but it is exactly the Dirichlet divisor problem; the plot is not undiscovered mathematics.

candidates.name: Gauss circle E(x)
candidates.note: A genuine non-zeta-looking 1/4 front, but the circle problem is a famous old problem, not a newly uncovered line.

candidates.name: Totient summatory Phi(x)
candidates.note: The 3/pi^2 level line is classical and overlaps the Farey/coprimality branch.

candidates.name: Normalized Mertens m(x)
candidates.note: Calmer than M(x), but it is still a standard Mobius summatory object and belongs to the logged Mertens family.

candidates.name: Dyadic-Mobius G2
candidates.verdict: PROJECT-NOVEL / not mathematically established as new
candidates.note: This is the most native unlogged transform in the batch. It is a new visualization here, but structurally it is a bounded dyadic transform of Mobius, so not an undiscovered theorem.

candidates.name: E2-invariance chip-order test
candidates.note: Useful as an instrument test: the square-root scale persists under these dyadic orders. That is a transform diagnostic, not a new critical line.

candidates.name: Chebyshev bias mod 4
candidates.note: The visual bias is real, but it is the classical Chebyshev/Rubinstein-Sarnak prime race.

candidates.name: Race family over moduli
candidates.note: Good calibration family; the direction and scale are part of known prime-race theory.

candidates.name: Liouville AP bias mod 4
candidates.note: It is an independent-looking bias plot, but lambda in arithmetic progressions is a classical multiplicative-function object.

candidates.name: Gap log-survival
candidates.note: The straight line is the null model itself; deviations are useful diagnostics, not an undiscovered line.

candidates.name: sum(g_n-log p_n) walk
candidates.note: The walk telescopes to p_k-2-theta(p_{k-1}); it is Chebyshev theta in gap coordinates.

candidates.name: Maximal-gap Cramer line
candidates.note: A legitimate frontier diagnostic, but Cramer/Granville maximal-gap behavior is already a named research area.

candidates.name: sum(Omega-omega)(n)
candidates.note: The constant-slope law is standard additive-function averaging; the residual is a calibration target.

candidates.name: Erdos-Kac balance
candidates.note: The slow convergence is visible; this is a textbook theorem-shaped control, not a new line.

candidates.name: k-free ladder
candidates.note: The slope constants and error hierarchy are classical; useful family visualization, not undiscovered.

candidates.name: Coprimality/Farey-count residual
candidates.note: This is the two-dimensional version of the totient-sum line, not a new branch distinct from #5.

candidates.name: Matrix critical width W
candidates.note: The contrast peaks when W has many small prime factors. That is local residue geometry, not an undiscovered critical line.

candidates.name: Bounded-CF / Zaremba dimension front
candidates.note: The threshold picture is meaningful, but it is the established Zaremba continued-fraction problem rather than an undiscovered line.
